Q: How do threat modeling and trust boundaries guide security controls for an AI app?
A:
Threat modeling identifies protected assets, actors, entry points, trust boundaries and harmful outcomes. It turns a vague instruction to 'secure the model' into testable controls around data access, external fetches, tool execution and output handling.

Treat model-generated arguments and retrieved instructions as untrusted at authority boundaries. Authentication, authorization, validation and audit are separate responsibilities. Prioritize controls according to actual paths and consequences, then test bypass attempts and recovery rather than relying on a safety prompt alone.
Why: A retrieved document tells an agent to upload customer records to a URL. The document may be readable evidence, but it has no authority to grant network destinations or permission to export private records.
Risk: Conflating readable content with executable authority creates an injection path.
Trade: Limit powerful operations and preserve useful read behavior behind explicit policy.
Try: Draw the boundary between retrieved text, proposed tool arguments and an authorized effect.
